This system aims to classify and contextualize diseases in relation to anatomical locations using a comprehensive ontology framework. The MOMS will allow healthcare professionals and researchers to explore relationships between diseases and anatomical locations, harnessing semantic web technologies and RDF data structures.

The system must accommodate a wide variety of diseases and anatomical locations, each represented by unique identifiers and labels. It should support the integration of multiple ontological databases, such as MONDO for diseases and UBERON for anatomical entities, using RDF schema standards for enhanced data interoperability.

MOMS will enable users to conduct complex queries to uncover patterns, correlations, and insights that can inform clinical practices and biomedical research. Additionally, the system will offer tools for ontology evolution, allowing healthcare professionals to update and refine classifications as new medical knowledge emerges. The platform will also facilitate data exchange between different healthcare systems and research institutions, promoting collaborative efforts in disease research and treatment development.
